raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through like I always do — what my wife and me can handle, what the land needs, what cash we've got.

---

**My thinking this year**

I'm 76 now, my wife is 73, and our son works in town — he comes back for Spring Festival and that's about it. So the two of us farm these 8 mu alone. I split it the way I've done for years: 5 mu of wheat-maize like most folks in the village, and 3 mu of cotton on the lighter ground. To be honest, my wife keeps telling me to give up the cotton — her back hurts from the picking — but the ginner in town still buys, so I keep it one more year.

The wheat went in last October, around the 10th, same as always. I put down about 40 kg of that DAP (18-46 stuff) per mu as base fertilizer. Now it's spring. The wheat is greening up nicely — not too yellow, not too dry — so around April when it starts jointing I'll topdress maybe 15 kg urea per mu and run the water. The tube well costs us about 20 yuan a mu each watering, electricity keeps going up. I water the wheat three times: once after the freeze, once at jointing with the topdress, once at heading. More than that is wasting money.

When wheat comes off in early June I hire the combine — 60 yuan a mu, it's worth it at my age. Then a neighbor helps me direct-seed maize into the stubble the next day. No tillage, no time for it. For maize I don't put much base down — half a bag of 15-15-15 compound per mu, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage. If the summer rains come I don't water; if it's dry around tasseling I'll water once.

Cotton I plant late April. Lumian 28, same as last few years — the seed shop in town has it. I do the planting by hand with my wife, takes us a week. About 50 kg of compound at planting and 10 kg of urea before flowering. Water it twice. For the picking in September-October I hire two village women for a few days — 100 yuan per day each, and that's cheap for what it is.

I don't use much spray. Cheap herbicide for weeds in the wheat and cotton, and that yellow-bottle insecticide when I see bollworm on the cotton. That's it.

All told I'll spend about 5000 yuan on everything. That's most of what we have. My son wires us a bit of money if it's tight. I'm not trying to make money off this land anymore — I just don't want to leave it bare, and the grain and cotton sales cover our food and some medicine.
